about: drawn after the maker's product photos of the Metal Arm (makermods.ai, 2026-11-12): the two jaws matte black resin, the cross beam black anodised aluminium, the linear guide rail on it bright ground steel.  The plain rail is drawn as that beam, and three things on it are the project's own drawing too, plain boxes and cylinders sized by eye from the photos, not MakerMods geometry: the steel guide rail as a strip 7 mm wide with rounded shoulders along the middle of the beam's top (bodies/makermods-metal/drawn-rail-steel.stl; the real rail is taller and carries the jaws on carriages, which are not drawn), its counterbored holes as dark discs every 15 mm (drawn-rail-bores.stl: the seven between the jaws, the two under the see-through jaw and the one in the open slot at the other jaw's back) and the beam's two end stops (drawn-end-stops.stl).  No gripper body, carriage, screw, camera mount or finger loop is drawn.

jaw-resin.evidence: the maker's own 3D viewer names the jaws matte resin beside black anodised links (roughness 0.8, no metal); the studio photo on grey and the station photo in daylight (photos 3 and 4 of the research notes): the jaws' lit faces read #636175 and #6a6571, a broad matt grey with lighter edges and no highlight, lighter than the anodised beam beside them (#312e3d and #18171c), and every black a little cool

beam-anodized.evidence: photos 3, 4 and 6: the beam reads #312e3d lit and #18171c to #272726 in shade, darker than the jaws beside it under the same light and with one broad soft sheen, no mirror image (satin, beside the glossier turned motor housing), so rougher than the base look; drawn here as a plain box, each of whose faces mirrors one patch of the room whole: with the base look's numbers its long faces, turned to a dark flag, read #0e0f16, darker than the film beside them (#111319), and its top, turned to a softbox, a mid grey lighter than the jaws; these numbers keep the box darker than the jaws at the homes and no face of it under the film

rail-ground.evidence: photos 1, 3 and 4: the rail reads #8a8589 to #aca7ae with its brightest tenth at #d7d3d9, bright steel but never white; drawn here as a strip whose flat top mirrors one patch of the room whole, and with the base look's numbers it read #f0f2f5 where that patch is a softbox, white on the card's light ground; a little rougher and dimmer, the top stays a grey under the photos' brightest tenth from every side
